correctness.rationale: Forcing chains cover the tree, with one initially blue endpoint per chain. A chain contains at most two pendant leaves; the cover by adjacent pairs of teeth, with a one-tooth path in odd order, attains the ceiling lower bound using the tree endpoint theorem. With even n every path must contain two leaves; a chain skipping an index would strand its internal pendant leaf as a singleton, so only the adjacent perfect pairing is possible. With odd n just one path has one leaf. If it has a spine endpoint, no two-leaf path can skip a tooth, so the sole unmatched tooth has odd index and gives the one spine choice. Otherwise either all paired paths are adjacent or exactly one pair skips one tooth and leaves its middle leaf as a singleton. That latter pattern is represented in the stated union by moving the unmatched choice to the selected outer endpoint. For counting distinct odd all-leaf choices, 00 cannot start a valid word. For prefix 10 or 01 the initial two entries can be deleted and prepended bijectively (when q=1 and the word starts 10, entry 3 is selected and can serve as the new singleton). For 11 one needs q=1 and entry 3 zero; there are 2^(m−1) remaining choices. With A₁=3 this yields the stated all-leaf, spine and total counts. The n=2 boundary gives the two endpoints of P₄.
residual_risks: The finite replay uses the immediate lower layer and the minimum layer; monotonicity excludes smaller layers in those instances. All-order completeness rests on the path argument, not extrapolation.
